## OBS-0002

REPDF's C9 files are not single-byte corruptions: each of the 100 C9 files differs from its original in 12-30 bytes spread across 11-28 distinct stream bodies (size unchanged). The paper only says C9 modifies 'a random byte within a zlib-compressed stream' (CLM-0026): that holds per damaged stream, but the paper does not say that 11-28 streams per file are hit.

- Result: C9/saveas diff_bytes 13/21/29, streams_hit 11/17/28; C9/print diff_bytes 12/22.5/30, streams_hit 12/18/26 (min/median/max). Replacement bytes are varied (top replacement byte covers <=4% of changes).

## OBS-0003

REPDF's C7 and C8 do not delete font data: they overwrite it in place with ASCII spaces (0x20), keeping the file size, so every xref offset stays valid. 100% of changed bytes are 0x20 in all 200 C7/C8 files.

Common Crawl's truncated PDF captures are usable natural pairs: for 34 of 35 length-truncated, refetched files in the SafeDocs 1k sample, the capture is an exact byte prefix of the complete refetched file; every capture is exactly 1,048,576 bytes.

## OBS-0300

In REPDF's C9 files, every damaged Flate stream carries exactly one changed byte, and a plain zlib inflate almost never notices it where it happens: 1220 of 1445 damaged streams (84%) decode to the end and fail only the Adler-32 check, 221 raise a decode error, 4 run out of input. A naive 'decode until error' salvage therefore emits wrong bytes in 1378 of 1445 streams (median 11,498 wrong bytes per stream). The median detection latency of 3,208 compressed bytes is over every stream that reports anything, Adler-only ones included (they report at the trailer); for the 221 streams that raise an inflate error the median is 5 bytes (OBS-1001).

- Result: damaged Flate streams 1445 in 100 files; changed bytes per damaged stream: 1 in all 1445. Outcome: check-only (zlib 'incorrect data check') 1220, data-error 221 (183 'invalid distance too far back'), incomplete 4. Detection latency (compressed bytes consumed past the changed byte when zlib reports an error or the check fails) n 1441, min/median/max 1/3208/2341864. Bytes emitted that differ from the original: median 11498, max 3670799; streams with any such bytes 1378. Verbatim decoded prefix as a fraction of the original's decoded length: median 0.4803. Rev 2 (2026-10-05, chair): re-run with flate_c9_probe.py rev 2, whose trim_eol keeps a CR that is the last zlib byte (OBS-1012); the 2026-09-27 rev 1 outputs (flate_c9_probe.*) stay committed because OBS-1012 pins them. Rev 1 had 1442 / 1217 / 1375 / median 3204 / 11426 / 0.48065; the 3 added streams are Adler-only (OBS-1012).

REPDF's C9 ('stream zlib') generator does not only damage Flate streams: of 2162 changed bytes across the 100 C9 files, 1446 fall in Flate stream spans (1445 in zlib data, one per damaged stream, and 1 in the CR of the CR LF before 'endstream'), 301 in other stream bodies (284 unfiltered, 17 DCTDecode), and 415 outside stream bodies (dictionaries, width arrays), in 99 of 100 files. ## OBS-0303

The producer's DEFLATE encoder can often be replayed exactly: 1124 of 2081 Flate streams (54%) in REPDF's Word 'Save As' originals are byte-identical to stock zlib level 6 output of their decoded data, but only 1 of 1344 in the 'Print to PDF' originals. For replayable streams, 're-encoding the candidate's decoded data reproduces the candidate exactly' is a far stronger correction oracle than Adler-32 alone.

- Result: stock_zlib_reproducible: saveas 1124 of 2081 streams byte-identical (all at level 6); print 1 of 1344 (level 6). Tested zlib.compress levels 0-9 with default window/memLevel/strategy (Python zlib 1.3). Streams = all Flate streams of the 100 originals that have a C9 counterpart.

## OBS-0501

Header loss alone (REPDF C1) makes the default Ghostscript 10.02.1 CLI fail on 100/100 files (the input is sniffed as PostScript); forcing the PDF interpreter recovers all 100, but adding xref loss (C1+C2 compound) makes forced Ghostscript fail on 100/100 while still exiting 0, matching the source rule that pdfi repair needs a '%PDF' somewhere in the file (CLM-0540). MuPDF recovers 100/100 in every variant; pdftotext 94/100 for header-damaged variants.

- Result: Recovered (extracted non-whitespace text >= 0.95 of the same tool's text from the original), out of 100 per variant. original: mutool 100, gs 100, gs forced 100, pdftotext 100 (qpdf exit 0 for all). C1: mutool 100, gs 0 (all nonzero exit, input treated as PostScript), gs forced 100, pdftotext 94 (6 Print-to-PDF files keep 79-90% of the text; in the one file inspected, pdftotext reported an xref reconstruction and a missing font resource), qpdf exit 3 (warnings) for all. C2: all four 100. C1+C2: mutool 100, gs 0, gs forced 0 with exit code 0 ('Catalog dictionary not located in file'), pdftotext 94, qpdf exit 3 for all. No file in C1 or C1+C2 contains '%PDF' anywhere.

Seeded smoke test of 16 engine runs (qpdf, pikepdf, MuPDF, PyMuPDF, pdf.js, PDFium, pdfcpu, PDFBox, Poppler, Ghostscript, lopdf, pdf-rs, hayro) on 2 corrupted REPDF files per class C1-C10 plus their 19 originals: every engine handles the originals; all fail C10 (partial cut) and C4 (page tree) except mutool clean on C4; no engine gets >= 95% of the original text back on any C9 or C10 file.

- Result: A smoke test, not a benchmark (n=2 per class). Produced output (definitions in the summary file) on the 19 originals: 19/19 for all 16 runs. Per class C1..C10 (out of 2): qpdf rewrite and pikepdf 2,2,2,0,1,2,2,2,2,0; mutool clean 2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,2,0 (C4 outputs have 1 page); PyMuPDF, pdf.js, PDFBox text, Ghostscript txtwrite, hayro 2,2,2,0,1,2,2,2,2,0; pypdfium2 and pdfcpu 0,2,2,0,1,2,2,2,2,0 (both reject header damage C1); pdftotext 2,2,2,0,1,0,2,2,2,0 (no text on C6); lopdf 0,2,2,0,0,2,2,2,2,0; pdf-rs (tolerant parse options) 0,0,0,0,0,0,2,2,2,0. Text ratio >= 0.95 of the original's characters: 0 files for every text engine on C9 and C10; pypdfium2 0/2 on C1; pdftotext 0/2 on C6; MuPDF text 1/2 on C7 and C8. One timeout (gs_text on a C9 file, 60 s); no negative exit codes (no crashes). C10 messages include 'unable to find trailer', 'startxref not found', 'Catalog dictionary not located'. 'Produced output' is not fidelity: mutool's C4 outputs keep 1 page.

## OBS-0702

Three conformance oracles disagree on the same files: on 35 repaired outputs (qpdf and mutool repairs of the 20 sampled corrupted files), 14 that `qpdf --check` passes and 13 that `pdfcpu validate -m strict` passes are non-compliant for the veraPDF Arlington checker; the Arlington checker also flags 13 of the 19 undamaged originals.

- Result: Originals (19): qpdf --check exit 0 on 19; pdfcpu strict valid 19, relaxed 19; Arlington 13 non-compliant, 6 compliant. Corrupted (20): qpdf --check exit 3 on 13, exit 2 on 7; pdfcpu strict 12 valid, relaxed 13; Arlington 16 not parsed, 2 non-compliant, 2 compliant. qpdf-repaired (20, 5 without output): qpdf --check exit 0 on 13, 2 on 2; pdfcpu strict 12, relaxed 15; Arlington 9 non-compliant, 6 compliant. mutool-repaired (20, 0 without output): qpdf --check exit 0 on 13, 2 on 7; pdfcpu strict 13, relaxed 15; Arlington 9 non-compliant, 6 compliant, 5 not parsed. Disagreements on repaired files: qpdf clean but Arlington non-compliant 14; pdfcpu strict valid but Arlington non-compliant 13; Arlington compliant but pdfcpu strict invalid 0. Because most undamaged originals already fail Arlington, a usable oracle must compare a repair against its original (delta), not use pass/fail alone (GAP-106).

## OBS-0703

On 676 Flate streams of 13 REPDF originals, stock zlib replays 228 of 333 Word 'Save As' streams byte-exactly (68%) but only 1 of 343 'Microsoft Print to PDF' streams; zlib-ng replays none of the Save As streams; preflate-rs reproduces 674 of 676 exactly. On 63 single-byte-damaged C9 streams, 54 (85.7%) fail only the Adler-32 check, and encoder replay places the first mismatch within 2 bytes of the flipped byte in only 4 of 22 cases.

- Result: Originals: print producer 343 streams, all FLEVEL 2; exact replay zlib 1, zlib-ng 1; preflate-rs ok 343, exact round trip 343, median corrections 125 bytes. Save As producer 333 streams, all FLEVEL 2; exact replay zlib 228 (68%; configs level 6 memLevel 9: 220, level 6 memLevel 8: 187, overlapping), zlib-ng 0; preflate-rs ok 331, round trip 331, median corrections 49 bytes. Damaged C9 streams (63, each with exactly 1 changed byte): zlib outcome 'incorrect data check' (Adler-32 only) 54, 'invalid distance too far back' 6, 'invalid literal/lengths set' 2, 'invalid bit length repeat' 1. Replay locator (22 damaged Save As streams with a replay config): first mismatch minus flip offset = -1304, 2054, -1, -5626, -211, -2, -54, -372, 1735, -124, -2965, -1550, -2938, -4453, -900, -2123, -92, -2974, -31, 50, 1, 0; within +-2 bytes in 4 of 22. preflate-rs on damaged streams: ok on 50 of 63 (all 50 are Adler-only; 0 of 9 hard errors); corrections larger than the original stream's in 39 of 50 (median ratio 1.84). Corroborates PR #16's 84.4% Adler-only share and extends OBS-0303 (54% replay on all Save As originals) with the producer split, zlib-ng and preflate-rs. Replay is a strong verifier (GAP-154) but a poor locator (GAP-150).

## OBS-0704

CPR's Step 1 (no LLM) produced text for all 20 sampled corrupted REPDF files but recovered fewer original words than simply opening the corrupted file with PyMuPDF on C1-C3, C7-C9; it beat that null baseline on C4, C6 and on one C5 file, and recovered no words of either C10 file.

- Result: Word recall (multiset share of the original's PyMuPDF words), CPR Step 1 vs null baseline (PyMuPDF on the corrupted file), per class, two files each: C1 0.747/0.818 vs null 1.0/1.0; C2 0.7096/0.7383 vs null 1.0/1.0; C3 0.7086/0.8215 vs null 1.0/1.0; C4 0.806/0.6946 vs null 0.0/0.0; C5 0.7888/0.7559 vs null 0.0/1.0; C6 0.7355/0.6861 vs null 0.0/0.0014; C7 0.7322/0.8119 vs null 0.9911/1.0; C8 0.5187/0.0 vs null 0.554/0.5261; C9 0.1195/0.5406 vs null 0.4996/0.7924; C10 0.0/0.0 vs null 0.0/0.0. With glyph names normalised, C10 rises to 0.514 and 0.1857 (CPR emits glyph names such as 'space' for unmapped codes). CER often exceeds 1 (duplicated or extra text, e.g. C8 4.75 and 7.59). rapidfuzz and jiwer CER agree on every file. About 3-24 s per file on 1 CPU. Step 2 (FontDB + llama3.1:8b) was not run. Linux run needed 28 Windows path literals patched in a temp copy (5 files) and fontTools' ttx on PATH.

## OBS-0705

gzrt's gzrecover gives no resynchronisation benefit on single-byte-damaged PDF Flate streams: on 54 Adler-only streams it emits wrong bytes in 9 and often stops early, and on 9 hard-error streams it recovers nothing in 8 and a shorter correct prefix than zlib in the ninth.

- Result: Same 63 damaged C9 streams as OBS-0703. Adler-only (54): gzrecover output contains wrong bytes in 9; raw zlib output contains wrong bytes in 53; gzrecover often stops early (0 bytes, or a 65,536-byte prefix). Hard errors (9): gzrecover recovered 0 bytes in 8; for object 1315 it emitted a 16,339-byte correct prefix where zlib's own prefix was 17,814 bytes. Its block-level restart (GAP-152) has nothing to restart at in single-block streams. GPL-2.0-or-later: run as a binary only.

## OBS-0706

CPU feasibility of the metric suite on the seeded sample: SSIM, pixel diff and LPIPS run in well under a second per page pair, but the MuPDF-vs-PDFium rendering floor on undamaged originals (SSIM down to 0.904) overlaps the damage signal of C7/C8, so visual scores must compare within one renderer; Tesseract (about 1 s/page) and docTR (about 6-7 s/page) OCR are both feasible on CPU.

- Result: Renderer floor (MuPDF vs PDFium, page 1, 72 dpi gray, 19 originals): SSIM min 0.9039, median 0.9414; share of pixels differing by > 32 levels max 0.0929; LPIPS (alex) max 0.0485. Original vs corrupted within one renderer: C6 SSIM 0.65-0.86, LPIPS 0.23-0.30; C7 SSIM 0.90-0.96, LPIPS 0.03-0.09; C8 SSIM 0.89-0.97, LPIPS 0.02-0.10; C9 SSIM 0.76-0.80, LPIPS 0.42-0.57. LPIPS about 0.17 s per pair on CPU (2 threads); docTR model load 2.2 s. OCR at 200 dpi vs PyMuPDF text layer (4 pages): Tesseract CER 0.0, 0.0385, 1.007, 0.0039 (1.0-1.3 s/page); docTR CER 0.0005, 0.0274, 1.007, 0.0044 (6.1-7.2 s/page); dinglehopper CER equals rapidfuzz CER on all 8. The two 1.007 values are not an OCR failure: that text+img page's text layer holds only part of the visible text (re-checked in OBS-0708). Structural diff (DeepDiff of `qpdf --json=2 --json-stream-data=none`, original vs qpdf-rewritten corrupted file, C2 and C7 picks): 0.08-1.3 s per file, but 147-4835 values_changed because a rewrite renumbers objects; a structural metric needs object-graph canonicalisation first.

On page 1 of the 19 sampled REPDF originals, Tesseract finds at least 1.25 times as many characters as the PDF text layer on 2 pages (1.99x and 1.70x, both from the Microsoft Print to PDF producer), and the print copy of a document can hold fewer text-layer characters than its Save As copy; a text-layer reference therefore undercounts the visible text on some originals.

- Result: Non-whitespace characters, page 1: PyMuPDF and PDFium text layers agree exactly on all 19 pages. OCR / text-layer ratio >= 1.25 on 2 pages: global_renewable_energy...(print) 747 vs 1487 (1.991, 55.3% of OCR words found in the layer) and UrbanRide_Electric_Bike_Scooter_Series(print) 596 vs 1013 (1.7, 66%). Below the flag: remote_work_home_office_guidelines(print) 952 vs 1144 (1.202) while its Save As copy's layer holds 1144; Evolution_Biodegradable_Plastics(print) 1639 vs 1722 while the Save As layer holds 1722. The other 15 pages are within 1.1x. Explains OBS-0706's CER 1.007 on both OCR engines. Implication for GAP-008: the reference for text metrics must be the upper bound (OCR or the Save As twin), not the print original's text layer alone.

## OBS-0800

Extending OBS-0201's truncation-pair check to ZIPs other than 0000.zip: the metadata layer (range-fetch first 2MB of the FULL cc-provenance-20230303.csv.gz, decompress, filter by zip-number embedded in file_name) and the zip-member layer (HEAD + central-directory read of a 1.6GB zip via HTTP range requests) both work correctly and quickly, confirming zips 0001/0002 hold both length-cap and rarer disconnect truncation rows (zip 0001 alone: 254 'length' + 1 'disconnect' REFETCHED_SUCCESS rows in the first 12,946-row metadata prefix). However every attempt to actually fetch the paired WARC capture from data.commoncrawl.org failed with HTTP 403 Forbidden (see CLM-0807/SRC-0811), so no prefix-match pairs from a non-0000 zip were obtained this session; two full-script runs (30 pairs across zips 0001/0002, and a reduced 6-pair single-zip run) both timed out (600s and 170s respectively) with zero completed rows, consistent with the per-request retry/backoff (20s/40s/60s) repeatedly firing on the 403s. The sampler design itself (stratified by zip and by truncation type, working within a <200MB budget) is validated as feasible; only the CC WARC-fetch step is currently blocked.

- Result: meta-prefix fetch: 1.33s for 2MB range -> 12,946 rows. zip 0001 central-directory open: 1.19s, 1 HTTP request, 1000 entries listed. zip-0001 rows available: 254 length-truncated + 1 disconnect-truncated (REFETCHED_SUCCESS). CC WARC range-fetch: HTTP 403 Forbidden (reproduced directly, tries=1, no retry). Net: 0 of the ~30 targeted pairs completed; sampler design confirmed workable, CC data-fetch step blocked as of 2026-09-27.
- Reproduce: `python3 research/experiments/cc_natural_pairs_other_zips.py --meta-bytes 2000000 --zips 0001,0002 --n-length-per-zip 13 --n-disconnect-per-zip 2 --workdir /tmp/cc-safedocs-otherzips --out research/experiments/results/cc_natural_pairs_other_zips.csv (timed out after 600s; diagnostic follow-up isolated the failing step to a single urllib Range GET against data.commoncrawl.org returning HTTP 403)`

## OBS-0900

Two-dummy-dictionary resync (CLM-0337) certifies bytes only at a confirmed restart point. Restarted at the 807 true DEFLATE block boundaries of 300 multi-block REPDF Flate streams (all Print to PDF), bytes identical under all-0x00 and all-0xFF dictionaries were always right (precision 1.0, median recall 0.816). A blind scan of the 2,048 bit offsets before each boundary instead found 51,120 false starts that inflate to the end, at 746 of 807 restarts, and they emit 8,521,181 bytes that are identical under both dictionaries yet wrong. Requiring the last block to end exactly at the Adler-32 trailer rejects every false start (0 of 51,120) and keeps 486 of 807 true starts. Extends PR #16, which found block-boundary resync nearly useless because most streams are a single block: where boundaries exist, dictionary invariance needs boundary confirmation to be grade 2.

- Result: streams_multiblock 300 (all print; no saveas stream had >1 block among those sampled); restarts 807, decoded_ok 807; precision_reliable 1.0; recall min/q1/median/q3/max 0.0147/0.4345/0.816/0.9245/0.996; recall in first 4 KiB 0.0059/0.2109/0.3645/0.561/0.9685; true start ends at trailer 486/807. ## OBS-0902

The pure-Rust DEFLATE encoders do not reproduce stock zlib output, so they cannot serve as the replay oracle. On 400 REPDF Save As streams that stock zlib 1.3 reproduces (level 6; memLevel 7: 179, memLevel 8: 221), zlib-rs 0.6.8 (through libz-rs-sys) at the same parameters matched 0 of 400, though it round-trips 400 of 400 (3,279,345 vs 3,242,574 bytes). miniz_oxide 0.9.1 at level 6 matched 5 of 400. zlib-rs output equals zlib-ng 2.2.5's on 380 of 400. A re-run on 2026-10-05 reproduced the 2026-09-27 output byte-for-byte. A pure-Rust replay oracle therefore cannot use a general-purpose Rust encoder. It needs a model of zlib 1.x deflate, and OBS-0908 shows that preflate-rs's token predictor already provides one (395/400). PR #16's mzbench uses miniz_oxide only to decode and is unaffected.

Identical on 2026-09-27 and 2026-10-05.

## OBS-0903

Encoder replay plus Adler-32 does not make a single-byte C9 correction unique. One Save As ToUnicode CMap stream (1,087 compressed bytes) has 3 single-byte candidates that pass inflate, Adler-32 and stock-zlib replay together: the true one, an Adler collision at byte 656, and a one-byte rewrite of the Adler trailer at byte 1084. The windowed search found only the trailer candidate and would have emitted it as 'unique'. Both wrong candidates yield malformed CMap lines (e.g. 5-hex-digit codes under a 2-byte codespace) that a grammar check rejects. Over 388 sampled damaged streams, replay localisation plus search fixed 196 of 266 Save As streams uniquely and correctly. Adler-32 algebra found the true literal in 21 of 317 streams that inflate to the end, and with perfect localisation (true position ±32) Adler alone was unique in 385 of 388. Corroborates PR #16's acceptance rule (Adler required, grammar tie-break, else Partial) and its trailer-damage false accept. Contradicts GAP-154's premise that a wrong correction almost never passes replay. PR #16's localisers (218/221 and 324/343) outperform both localisers tried here.

- Result: 388 streams (every 3rd damaged stream <= 32 KiB compressed; 266 saveas, 122 print), wall 723.9 s. saveas: original replayable 266/266, true position in replay window 185, method unique+correct (replay) 196, wrong replay-unique emission 1. print: replayable 0, method unique+correct (Adler) 10/122. All: true in Adler-algebra positions 21 (of 317 that inflate to the end); oracle window (+-32) Adler counts {1: 385, 2: 3}; exhaustive search of 63 saveas streams <= 1,536 B: 62 unique+correct, 1 with 3 candidates under both Adler and replay; localisation offset min/median/max -24052/-8/487; median search 1.125 s, max 25 s.

## OBS-0904

Of the 820 C9 damaged streams whose originals stock zlib replays (all Save As), 87 (10.6%) are themselves canonical zlib streams; in 85 of them the damage is outside the trailer. For these streams, zlib re-compression of their own wrong output reproduces the damaged body byte-for-byte, so only the Adler-32 trailer betrays the damage and replay has nothing to localise. Rewriting the trailer passes inflate, Adler-32 and replay at once. That rewrite needs 1 trailer byte in 3 streams, 2 bytes in 1, 3 bytes in 54 and 4 bytes in 29, so a single-byte search meets it in 3 streams (one is the OBS-0903 case). Extends PR #16's note that one Adler false accept came from trailer damage: replay does not close that hole, and a body hypothesis must be preferred over a trailer hypothesis by an explicit damage prior or a grammar check, not by the oracles.

- Result: replayable damaged streams 820 (saveas); damage in trailer 2; damaged inflates to end 672; damaged body replay-consistent 87 (85 excluding trailer damage); trailer bytes to rewrite {1: 3, 2: 1, 3: 54, 4: 29}.

## OBS-0905

Each of the 100 REPDF object_header files has one 8-byte deletion (an 'N 0 obj' header plus EOL) and an unchanged xref. A small constraint model over the stale xref offsets restores the original byte-for-byte in all 100. The unknowns are deletion point, length and producer offset bias, constrained by startxref, /Prev and /XRefStm and by the missing header. z3 5.1.0 and plain enumeration agree in 100/100, finding L = 8 and the bias uniquely in a median of 0.05 to 0.15 s. The byte-exact restoration also needs the file's EOL style to fill the gap, since the EOL bytes alone are ambiguous. Every Print to PDF file has bias +1 (each xref offset points at the EOL byte before 'N 0 obj'), and every Save As file has bias 0. Extends PR #16's offset heuristics (lopdf's ±64-byte correction, qpdf's header rebase, qpdf #341's off-by-one startxref) with an exact restoration. No SMT solver is needed in the engine.

- Result: print 50 and saveas 50: one missing header 50/50; z3 (L, c) unique 50/50; L = true 8 50/50; z3 agrees with brute force 50/50; byte-exact restoration among candidates 50/50; unique distinct restoration 0/50 (EOL fill ambiguous); EOL-style choice byte-exact 50/50; bias c = 1 for 50/50 print, c = 0 for 50/50 saveas; median z3 0.047 s (print) / 0.07 s (saveas), brute force 0.147 s / 0.06 s.

## OBS-0906

This is the first test of GAP-205 on PDFs. The glyph codes of 39 REPDF Print to PDF originals were treated as a substitution cipher, with no ToUnicode, no font program and no widths. The decoder used a character 4-gram model trained only on 29 cached open-access paper texts, plus simulated annealing. Across 664 per-font slots it decoded 76.6% of 192,680 in-alphabet code occurrences correctly. Accuracy rose to 0.86 for slots of 1,024 to 4,096 codes and was about 0.44 to 0.49 for slots under 256 codes. Digits were almost never recovered (6.5% of 2,714). Abstaining on low-margin codes keeps 86.8% of tokens at 86.3% accuracy. Decipherment is thus feasible for long Latin slots. For digits and short slots it fabricates (GAP-201), so its output can be grade 4 at best, with per-code margins and abstention. It does not yet use PR #16's width-vector fingerprints (widths.py).

- Result: files 39; slots 664; tokens scored (in-alphabet truth) 192,680, token accuracy 0.7657, median slot accuracy 0.761; truth outside the 90-symbol alphabet 61,885 (unscored); digits 2,714 at 0.0652. By slot length: 8-64 codes 0.490 (169 slots), 64-256 0.439 (173), 256-1024 0.746 (257), 1024-4096 0.858 (65). Abstention (margin > 0/2/5/10): coverage 0.938/0.920/0.898/0.868, accuracy on kept 0.813/0.827/0.843/0.863. Latin-only slots (347): 0.764, digits 0.104. LM 1,636,841 training chars; iterations max(6000, 150 x codes), 3 restarts. Shards ran about 600-680 s each on 2 CPUs.

## OBS-0907

In all 50 REPDF Print to PDF originals, every one of 889 page-font objects has an anonymous BaseFont (CIDFont+F1..F22). Each still embeds a TrueType program whose 'name' table keeps the real family name (889/889; 40 families, e.g. Cambria, Rubik Medium, Noto Serif Thin, MaoKenWangXingYuan). 879 also keep a usable cmap, and every font has a ToUnicode CMap that agrees with the cmap-derived map on 35,673 of 35,792 shared codes. ## OBS-0908

A pure-Rust encoder-replay oracle already exists inside preflate-rs 0.7.6 (Microsoft, Apache-2.0, unsafe forbidden). Its token predictor, given zlib level-6 parameters (lazy 8/16, chain 128, nice 128, TOO_FAR 4096, memLevel 7 or 8) and ZERO corrections, re-encodes the plaintext into the original stream byte-for-byte for 395 of 400 REPDF Save As streams that stock zlib reproduces (memLevel 8: 220, memLevel 7: 175). It misses 4 memLevel-7 streams (cause not investigated), and its analyser fails on 1 (PredictionFailure). With its own estimated parameters and zero corrections it reproduces only 47 of 399, so the parameters must come from a producer profile, not from per-stream estimation. Print to PDF streams stay out of reach: 0 of 400 under zlib-6 parameters or their own estimates. Preflate fingerprints that encoder as a zlib-like lazy matcher (good 8, lazy 16, nice 128, chain about 100) that allows matches to the stream start and very far matches, which zlib forbids. Their correction blobs have a median of 98 bytes (about 2.1% of compressed bytes overall), against 24 for Save As. Forcing parameters made preflate-rs panic 14 times (index out of bounds in tree_predictor.rs) on print plaintexts, so an engine must isolate it or fix the panic. This revises OBS-0902: a pure-Rust replay oracle does not need a new zlib port. It extends agent B's preflate-rs entry (round trip with corrections, correction size as a damage signal) and the plan's GAP-154.

- Result: Save As (400, all stock-zlib replayable): zero-correction replay with zlib-6 parameters exact 395 (memLevel 8: 220, 7: 175), miss 4, analysis error 1; own estimated parameters exact 47. Print (400, none stock-zlib replayable): 0 exact either way. Round trip with corrections: 799/800 exact. CABAC correction blob median 24 B (Save As) vs 98 B (Print); totals 26,723 B over 3,237,326 compressed B vs 366,178 B over 17,779,688 B. preflate-rs panics caught: 14.

## OBS-1012

PR #16's 1,445 damaged C9 Flate streams contain all 1,442 of OBS-0300's, with the same inflate outcome for every one. The 3 extra streams (2 fonts, 1 content stream, all Adler-only, all Print to PDF) end in a zlib byte 0x0D followed by a single LF before 'endstream'; flate_c9_probe.py's trim_eol strips CR LF, cuts off the last Adler-32 byte, finds the original does not inflate to the end and skips the stream. OBS-0300/0301/0302 therefore undercount damaged Flate streams by 3 (1,442 vs 1,445; 1,217 vs 1,220 Adler-only), and those 3 bytes are OBS-0302's 'FlateDecode (does not inflate cleanly in the original)'.

## OBS-1013

Explains OBS-1007 and corrects a detail of CLM-1028. Among the 245 Adler-only C9 streams of at most 4 KiB, 2 have their damage in the Adler-32 trailer (unfixable by a data-only search). ## OBS-1104

REPDF's C7 and C8 files keep no embedded font program anywhere in the file, not even as unreferenced objects, and C8 also keeps no CMap stream; C6 keeps nearly all programs and ToUnicode maps. So in C8 only font names, encodings, widths and the content-stream codes survive, and glyph-shape recovery has nothing to read. Separately, leaving one Save As base document out, 93.1% of its ToUnicode entries (font name without subset tag, code) also occur in the other 49 documents' maps, and 94.0% of those agree: a mapping fitted on other base documents decodes most of a held-out document, so a split by base document alone does not hold font knowledge out.

- Result: Totals over 50 files per cell (all indirect objects, referenced or not). Save As: originals 2,130 font dicts, 618 with ToUnicode, 1,512 program references, 948 program streams (/Length1 or CFF/OpenType subtype), 618 CMap streams; C6 2,085 / 606 / 1,479 / 926 / 606; C7 2,130 / 618 / 0 / 0 / 769; C8 2,130 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0. Print to PDF: originals 889 / 889 / 889 / 889 / 889; C6 identical to originals; C7 1,778 / 1,778 / 0 / 0 / 889; C8 1,778 / 0 / 0 / 0 / 0. Leave-one-document-out ToUnicode overlap, Save As: 32,475 entries, 30,236 (93.11%) covered by the same font name in other documents, 93.97% of covered entries agree; per document 85.0-96.7% covered (median 93.7%); all 50 documents have covered entries. Print to PDF names fonts CIDFont+F<n>, a per-document index, so its figure (80.8% covered, 73.2% agree) measures code reuse under anonymous names and is not a font-identity result. Entries are counted per map entry, not weighted by text frequency.
- Reproduce: `cd research/experiments/stage4-contrarian && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 timeout 600 nice -n 10 python3 font_inventory.py /home/user/dfrc-korea/repdf results/font_inventory`

## OBS-1203

MuPDF 1.28.5 (the WP-3.1 pin) extracts less text than 1.28.0 from two header-damaged (C1) REPDF files, and `mutool draw -F txt` exits 1 on both. The conda-forge build of 1.28.0 and a source build of 1.28.0 made the same way give identical results, so the cause is the version, not the build.

- Result: Lumina (Save As, C1): 1.28.0 conda and 1.28.0 source rc 0, 9,205 text bytes; 1.28.5 rc 1, 4,500 bytes. global_cloud (Print, C1): 1.28.0 conda and source rc 0, 4,804 bytes; 1.28.5 rc 1, 3,609 bytes. PyMuPDF 1.28.2 opens both without an error: 6 pages and 6,237 / 3,301 characters. PyMuPDF uses a different extraction path, so this only suggests the change came after 1.28.2. Consequence for WP-3.1: pin MuPDF 1.28.0, or keep 1.28.5 and record this C1 regression as a known difference.

## OBS-1214

PR #16's mid-size unlocalised Adler-only search (CLM-1019) was re-run on two stride-10 samples of the rebuilt 1,445-case set, with a 20 s budget per case. Phase 0 is OBS-1010's sample and phase 5 is new. Phase 0 reproduces OBS-1010 exactly: 28 of 47 fixed, all byte-exact, 19 timeouts. Phase 5 fixes 35 of 48 (13 timeouts). Pooled, that is 63 of 95 (66.3%, Wilson 95% interval 56.3-75.0%), against CLM-1019's 158 of 239 (66.1%).

- Result: phase 0: cases 47, fixed 28, exact 28, timeouts 19, notfound 0, search p50 14.75 s, wall 9m14s. phase 5: cases 48, fixed 35, exact 35, timeouts 13, notfound 0, p50 9.28 s, wall 8m20s. Load 2.0 at start, 4.2-5.3 at the end. Pooled 63/95 = 0.663 (Wilson 0.563-0.750); CLM-1019 158/239 = 0.661 (Wilson 0.599-0.718). The intervals overlap and the point estimates agree within 0.2 points.

## OBS-1215

OBS-0906's glyph-code decipherer is deterministic, but its stored command is not reproducible as written. It trains the language model on every *.txt in research/cache/fulltext, a gitignored cache that other agents add to. On 2026-10-05 that directory held 33 texts, 4 more than the 29 the stored run used. Re-run on all 33, overall token accuracy is 0.7486 against the stored 0.7657, and 400 of 664 slots change. Re-run on exactly the 29 texts of the stored manifest, every value in the summary and all 664 CSV rows are identical to OBS-0906's. The LM corpus must be pinned by manifest for this result to be reproducible.
